section13_checks.prohibition_description: Treating Grant Agreement Annex templates as the governing structural schema for proposal writing.
Inventing call constraints, scope requirements, expected outcomes, or expected impacts not present in Tier 2B.
Inventing project facts (partners, capabilities, roles, objectives, budget figures) not present in Tier 3.
Commencing Phase 8 activity before the budget gate (Phase 7) has passed.
Storing durable decisions only in agent memory without writing them to Tier 4.
Allowing a workflow or skill to become a de facto constitutional authority.
Silently reordering phases or weakening gate conditions.
Finalizing proposal text when source state is incomplete, contradictory, or unvalidated, without flagging the gap.
Using agent-local knowledge of Horizon Europe rules as a substitute for reading Tier 1 source documents.
Producing Tier 5 outputs not traceable to specific inputs in Tier 1–4.
Modifying Tier 1 or Tier 2 source documents to reflect project-specific assumptions.
Treating CLAUDE.md as advisory or optional.

check_notes.13.1: Structural authority is Tier 2A section_schema_registry.json (RIA); instrument_sections_addressed cite application-form sections A.4, B.3, B.3.1, B.3.2. 'grant agreement' appears only as the instrument the consortium agreement complements, and 'extended annex' refers to an ethics annex, not a schema source. No Grant Agreement Annex, AGA template, or MGA annex is used as a structural schema.
check_notes.13.2: Call-requirement claims (open-science scope, eligibility on European EO programmes, harmonisation) carry Tier 2B references: traceability_footer cites scope_requirements.json (SR-04, SR-05) and call_constraints.json (CC-08); governance_matrix source_basis repeats them. The skill does not read Tier 2B directly; it confirms the artifact supplies the references.
check_notes.13.3: Partner identifiers (P01–P12), roles, and WP leads carry Tier 3/Tier 4 references: partners.json, roles.json, and phase3 wp_structure.json in the traceability footer and per-body source_basis. Fictional partners are explicitly declared Assumed (R04), consistent with §13.3 flagging of partial population rather than fabrication passed as fact.
check_notes.13.4: Not a Phase 8 artifact (schema_id orch.phase6.implementation_architecture.v1). No budget figures asserted; R12 explicitly states the repository computes no figure for this lump-sum topic per §8.1. No '€[0-9]+' or person-month cost values used as confirmed budget claims.
check_notes.13.5: Not verifiable from artifact content alone; enforced by the decision-log-update skill. Recorded pass for non-applicability at artifact level.
check_notes.13.6: Not verifiable from an artifact. Recorded pass for non-applicability at artifact level.
check_notes.13.7: Phase 6 artifact references only earlier-phase inputs (phase3 wp_structure.json), which are legitimate Phase 6 inputs per §7. No reference to Phase 7 or 8 outputs as inputs.
check_notes.13.8: Structurally a Tier 4 phase output, not a Tier 5 deliverable, so the unresolved-status flagging check does not apply. Where source state is thin, the artifact flags it openly (ethics_assessment notes the missing Tier 2B gender-exemption source and defers to Phase 8), consistent with honest gap declaration.
check_notes.13.9: Regulatory claims (ethics self-assessment, civil-focus, gender equality plan, gender dimension) each carry Tier 1 references; traceability_footer cites implementation_constraints.json with matching relevant_fields. The skill does not read Tier 1 directly; it confirms the artifact supplies the references.
check_notes.13.10: Structurally a Tier 4 phase output, not a Tier 5 artifact; the no_unsupported_claims_declaration / claim_statuses check does not apply. The artifact nonetheless carries a full tiered traceability footer.
